title: Cheap-signal deterministic rule candidates and NEW closed-form series composites (IndEgo gold-150, LOCO)
determinism: no learned weights; per-fold direction from the training-clip AUROC sign; thresholds = quantiles p01/p05/p10/p25 (mirrored) of TRAINING clips, quantised to 4 dp; integer Q=4 comparisons (thresholds_q = int(round(t*1e4))); indicator = any rung crossed; severity = integer count of rungs crossed; RNG only in the seeded clip bootstrap

data.window: 10 s, 100 frames decoded at 160x90 (P_nframes=100 for all 150)

protocol.in_domain: leave-one-clip-out over the 7 IndEgo clips; direction+thresholds from the 6 training clips only
protocol.indicator: score >= 1 rung crossed (comparable to Q1 per-rule indicator AUROC)

device: CPU only (no GPU; torch present but unused)

candidates.derivation: mean |DCT| energy outside the top-left 8x8 block; drops when the frame is defocused/motion-blurred, rises with sensor/compression noise
std over frames of the per-frame HF DCT energy; unstable HF energy despite static content = coding noise/flicker
mean number of exported motion vectors per decoded frame; motion-vector count is encoder flow activity, high = busy camera/hands
variance of the Laplacian (raw sharpness units, window mean); the classic focus measure
Haar HH (diagonal) sub-band energy share; diagonal detail is the first thing blur removes
closed form: mean_t |lap_var(t)-lap_var(t-1)| / (mean_t lap_var(t)+1e-6); relative frame-to-frame sharpness instability (focus hunting / rolling-shutter strobe) at zero extra decode cost
mean over frames of phase-correlation shift vs the first frame (px at 160x90); accumulated viewpoint displacement
per-frame mean high-frequency DCT energy averaged over the 100-frame series (same quantity as B_dct_hfenergy but series-averaged)
data-driven motion floor of diff_e (median+MAD of the window); the window's own noise/jitter level
candidates.verdict_reason: same rule NO_ACTIVE_WORK already at 0.695; rho=0.97 with the Q1 feature

candidates.derivation: log-log FFT power-spectrum slope; steeper (more negative) = energy concentrated at low frequencies = blurred
median global (phase-correlation) shift magnitude in px; large = camera/ego motion, near-zero = static viewpoint
slope of radially averaged power spectrum; flatter spectra (less negative) carry relatively more high-frequency energy
candidates.verdict_reason: same rule BLUR already at 0.695; rho=0.90 with the Q1 feature

candidates.derivation: share of FFT power above the mid band; a flat/smooth image loses high frequencies
max over frames of the shift vs the first frame; a single jump (scene change / hard cut)
Haar HL (vertical-edge) sub-band energy share; vertical edges vanish under horizontal motion blur
closed form: d=diff_e series, F=median(d)+MAD(d) (per-window noise floor), value=mean(max(d-F,0))/(F+1e-6); how far motion spikes rise ABOVE the window's own noise floor, not how often
fraction of frames with diff_e above the window's median+MAD floor; duty cycle of real motion
Haar LH (horizontal-edge) sub-band energy share; horizontal edges vanish under vertical motion blur
share of motion energy in the top PCA component; a single dominant translation = clean ego-motion
closed form: F=median(diff_e)+MAD(diff_e); value=mean_t[ d_t>F and d_{t-1}<=F ]; rate of activity onsets per frame (burst/gap statistic)
longest run of frames with diff_e below the floor, as a fraction of the window; high = long dead time
fraction of packets that are non-key frames; low means the encoder keeps re-sending I-frames (scene cuts/hard changes) or almost no coded frames
std of all packet sizes / mean, i.e. bitrate instability across the window; a flickering/duplicated/strobing source spends unevenly
mean I-frame packet size (bytes) over the window; large I-frames at fixed CRF mean fine detail/noise, tiny/zero means no intra refresh or a blank keyframe

closed form: ac1(x)=sum((x_t-m)(x_{t-1}-m))/sum((x_t-m)^2); value=ac1(diff_e)-ac1(luma_mean); motion that is bursty while luma is static gives a positive contrast (handheld jitter / strobing), smooth global motion drives both together
dominant temporal period (frames) of the luma signal; a fixed period indicates a loop/repeat rather than live work
peak normalised autocorrelation of the luma_mean series (lag>=1); high = the window's brightness pattern repeats
mean dHash Hamming distance of consecutive frames (GPU window aggregate)
candidates.verdict_reason: only 1 distinct values on gold-150 (constant: cannot threshold)

candidates.derivation: GPU flicker index (illumination instability)
candidates.verdict_reason: only 1 distinct values on gold-150 (constant: cannot threshold)

candidates.derivation: closed form: mean_t under_frac(t) + mean_t over_frac(t) with under=luma<0.05, over=luma>0.95; total hard-clipped area, direction-free (fails either way)

closed form: Wiener entropy of the diff_e spectrum, exp(mean(log(P+1e-12)))/mean(P+1e-12) over rfft bins 1..T/2; ~0 = tonal/periodic motion (oscillation, strobe), ~1 = broadband noise motion (coding noise / shake)
self zero-normalised cross-correlation of the window against its own frames; high = the window repeats its own content
mean P-frame bytes / mean I-frame bytes; high = inter frames nearly as expensive as intra = high residual/noise, low = static over-compressed scene
mean P-frame packet size (bytes); P bytes rise with residual motion and coding noise at fixed quality
residual of the dominant affine/PCA motion model; high = motion the global model cannot explain (independent object/hand motion)

new_composites_closed_form.P_motion_excess_nf: closed form: d=diff_e series, F=median(d)+MAD(d) (per-window noise floor), value=mean(max(d-F,0))/(F+1e-6); how far motion spikes rise ABOVE the window's own noise floor, not how often
new_composites_closed_form.P_ac1_contrast: closed form: ac1(x)=sum((x_t-m)(x_{t-1}-m))/sum((x_t-m)^2); value=ac1(diff_e)-ac1(luma_mean); motion that is bursty while luma is static gives a positive contrast (handheld jitter / strobing), smooth global motion drives both together
new_composites_closed_form.P_clip_total: closed form: mean_t under_frac(t) + mean_t over_frac(t) with under=luma<0.05, over=luma>0.95; total hard-clipped area, direction-free (fails either way)
new_composites_closed_form.P_sharp_flicker: closed form: mean_t |lap_var(t)-lap_var(t-1)| / (mean_t lap_var(t)+1e-6); relative frame-to-frame sharpness instability (focus hunting / rolling-shutter strobe) at zero extra decode cost
new_composites_closed_form.P_motion_tonality: closed form: Wiener entropy of the diff_e spectrum, exp(mean(log(P+1e-12)))/mean(P+1e-12) over rfft bins 1..T/2; ~0 = tonal/periodic motion (oscillation, strobe), ~1 = broadband noise motion (coding noise / shake)
new_composites_closed_form.P_burst_onset_rate: closed form: F=median(diff_e)+MAD(diff_e); value=mean_t[ d_t>F and d_{t-1}<=F ]; rate of activity onsets per frame (burst/gap statistic)
new_composites_closed_form.P_series_luma_mean: context denominator only: mean luma_mean over the 100-frame series
new_composites_closed_form.P_series_diff_e_mean: context denominator only: mean diff_e over the 100-frame series

limitations: n=150 with only 7 clips; clip bootstrap has 7 resample units, so CIs are wide and the indicator AUROC is a coarse statistic (binary).
Direction is chosen inside each fold from training labels (that is LOCO-honest but means the reported direction can differ from a physical prior).
Severity AUROC and indicator AUROC rank differently when a feature's tail is informative but its bulk is not.
The frozen_thresholds_* fields are fitted on all 7 clips (what a deployment table would carry); they are NOT used for the LOCO columns.
0.5-granularity: with a binary indicator the AUROC is determined by TPR/FPR at one operating point (equivalent to balanced accuracy), which is why Q1 per-rule values sit near 0.5.
No OOD labels were read for this experiment; no hold-out 108 windows were touched.
